<search shelf=wiki>A Professional Engineer must certify our Plan unless the qualified-facilities section lets us self-certify. As a self-certified Tier II facility, above what aggregate aboveground capacity must we switch to an engineer-certified Plan?</search>= 3 notes
  [2bc] page · 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements. — when: You need what section 112.6 requires: Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.
  [r2s] page · 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan. — when: You need what section 112.3 requires: Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.
  [1dh] page · 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities). — when: You need what section 112.9 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).
<open>2bc</open>= 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements. — Section 112.6 of the regulation — Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.
  §text Qualified facilities meeting the Tier I applicability criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1) are subject to the requirements in paragraph (a) of this section. Qualified facilities meeting the Tier II applicability criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2) are subject to the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section.
  §a (a) Tier I Qualified Facilities—(1) Preparation and Self-Certification of the Plan. If you are an owner or operator of a facility that meets the Tier I qualified facility criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1), you must either: comply with the requirements of paragraph (a)(3) of this section; or prepare and implement a Plan meeting requirements of paragraph (b) of this section; or prepare and implement a Plan meeting the general Plan requirements in [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and applicable requirements in subparts B and C, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d). If you do not follow the appendix G template, you must prepare an equivalent Plan that meets all of the applicable requirements listed in this part, and you must supplement it with a section cross-referencing the location of requirements listed in this part and the equivalent requirements in the other prevention plan. To complete the template in appendix G, you must certify that:
  §i (i) You are familiar with the applicable requirements of 40 CFR part 112;
  §ii (ii) You have visited and examined the facility;
  §iii (iii) You prepared the Plan in accordance with accepted and sound industry practices and standards;
  §iv (iv) You have established procedures for required inspections and testing in accordance with industry inspection and testing standards or recommended practices;
  §v (v) You will fully implement the Plan;
  §vi (vi) The facility meets the qualification criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1);
  §vii (vii) The Plan does not deviate from any requirement of this part as allowed by [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and 112.7(d) or include measures pursuant to [1dh] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping; and
  §viii (viii) The Plan and individual(s) responsible for implementing this Plan have the approval of management, and the facility owner or operator has committed the necessary resources to fully implement this Plan.
  §viii-2 (2) Technical Amendments. You must certify any technical amendments to your Plan in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section when there is a change in the facility design, construction, operation, or maintenance that affects its potential for a discharge as described in [7pp] 112.1 General applicability.(b). If the facility change results in the facility no longer meeting the Tier I qualifying criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1) because an individual oil storage container capacity exceeds 5,000 U.S. gallons or the facility capacity exceeds 10,000 U.S. gallons in aggregate aboveground storage capacity, within six months following preparation of the amendment, you must either:
  §viii-2-i (i) Prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with [2bc] 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.(b) if you meet the Tier II qualified facility criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2); or
  §viii-2-ii (ii) Prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with the general Plan requirements in [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., and applicable requirements in subparts B and C, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d).
  §viii-3 (3) Plan Template and Applicable Requirements. Prepare and implement an SPCC Plan that meets the following requirements under [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and in subparts B and C of this part: introductory paragraph of §[m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., 112.7(a)(3)(i), 112.7(a)(3)(iv), 112.7(a)(3)(vi), 112.7(a)(4), 112.7(a)(5), 112.7(c), 112.7(e), 112.7(f), 112.7(g), 112.7(k), 112.8(b)(1), 112.8(b)(2), 112.8(c)(1), 112.8(c)(3), 112.8(c)(4), 112.8(c)(5), 112.8(c)(6), 112.8(c)(10), 112.8(d)(4), 112.9(b), 112.9(c)(1), 112.9(c)(2), 112.9(c)(3), 112.9(c)(4), 112.9(c)(5), 112.9(d)(1), 112.9(d)(3), 112.9(d)(4), 112.10(b), 112.10(c), 112.10(d), 112.12(b)(1), 112.12(b)(2), 112.12(c)(1), 112.12(c)(3), 112.12(c)(4), 112.12(c)(5), 112.12(c)(6), 112.12(c)(10), and 112.12(d)(4). The template in appendix G to this part has been developed to meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 112 and, when completed and signed by the owner or operator, may be used as the SPCC Plan. Additionally, you must meet the following requirements:
  §viii-3-i (i) Failure analysis, in lieu of the requirements in [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(b). Where experience indicates a reasonable potential for equipment failure (such as loading or unloading equipment, tank overflow, rupture, or leakage, or any other equipment known to be a source of discharge), include in your Plan a prediction of the direction and total quantity of oil which could be discharged from the facility as a result of each type of major equipment failure.
  §viii-3-ii (ii) Bulk storage container secondary containment, in lieu of the requirements in §[737] 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).(c)(2) and (c)(11) and 112.12(c)(2) and (c)(11). Construct all bulk storage container installations (except mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks), including mobile or portable oil storage containers, so that you provide a secondary means of containment for the entire capacity of the largest single container plus additional capacity to contain precipitation. Dikes, containment curbs, and pits are commonly employed for this purpose. You may also use an alternative system consisting of a drainage trench enclosure that must be arranged so that any discharge will terminate and be safely confined in a catchment basin or holding pond. Position or locate mobile or portable oil storage containers to prevent a discharge as described in [7pp] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §viii-3-iii (iii) Overfill prevention, in lieu of the requirements in §[737] 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).(c)(8) and 112.12(c)(8). Ensure that each container is provided with a system or documented procedure to prevent overfills of the container, describe the system or procedure in the SPCC Plan and regularly test to ensure proper operation or efficacy.
  §b (b) Tier II Qualified Facilities—(1) Preparation and Self-Certification of Plan. If you are the owner or operator of a facility that meets the Tier II qualified facility criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2), you may choose to self-certify your Plan. You must certify in the Plan that:
  §i-2 (i) You are familiar with the requirements of this part;
  §ii-2 (ii) You have visited and examined the facility;
  §iii-2 (iii) The Plan has been prepared in accordance with accepted and sound industry practices and standards, and with the requirements of this part;
  §iv-2 (iv) Procedures for required inspections and testing have been established;
  §v-2 (v) You will fully implement the Plan;
  §vi-2 (vi) The facility meets the qualification criteria set forth under [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2);
  §vii-2 (vii) The Plan does not deviate from any requirement of this part as allowed by [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and 112.7(d) or include measures pursuant to [1dh] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping, except as provided in paragraph (b)(3) of this section; and
  §viii-4 (viii) The Plan and individual(s) responsible for implementing the Plan have the full approval of management and the facility owner or operator has committed the necessary resources to fully implement the Plan.
  §viii-2-2 (2) Technical Amendments. If you self-certify your Plan pursuant to paragraph (b)(1) of this section, you must certify any technical amendments to your Plan in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section when there is a change in the facility design, construction, operation, or maintenance that affects its potential for a discharge as described in [7pp] 112.1 General applicability.(b), except:
  §viii-2-i-2 (i) If a Professional Engineer certified a portion of your Plan in accordance with paragraph (b)(4) of this section, and the technical amendment affects this portion of the Plan, you must have the amended provisions of your Plan certified by a Professional Engineer in accordance with paragraph (b)(4)(ii) of this section.
  §viii-2-ii-2 (ii) If the change is such that the facility no longer meets the Tier II qualifying criteria in [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2) because it exceeds 10,000 U.S. gallons in aggregate aboveground storage capacity you must, within six months following the change, prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with the general Plan requirements in [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and the applicable requirements in subparts B and C of this part, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d).
  §viii-3-2 (3) Applicable Requirements. Except as provided in this paragraph, your self-certified SPCC Plan must comply with [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and the applicable requirements in subparts B and C of this part:
  §viii-3-i-2 (i) Environmental Equivalence. Your Plan may not include alternate methods which provide environmental equivalence pursuant to [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2), unless each alternate method has been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-3-ii-2 (ii) Impracticability. Your Plan may not include any determinations that secondary containment is impracticable and provisions in lieu of secondary containment pursuant to [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d), unless each such determination and alternate measure has been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-3-iii-2 (iii) Produced Water Containers. Your Plan may not include any alternative procedures for skimming produced water containers in lieu of sized secondary containment pursuant to [1dh] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6), unless they have been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-4-2 (4) Professional Engineer Certification of Portions of a Qualified Facility's Self-Certified Plan.
  §viii-4-i (i) As described in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, the facility owner or operator may not self-certify alternative measures allowed under [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) or (d), that are included in the facility's Plan. Such measures must be reviewed and certified, in writing, by a licensed Professional Engineer. For each alternative measure allowed under [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2), the Plan must be accompanied by a written statement by a Professional Engineer that states the reason for nonconformance and describes the alternative method and how it provides equivalent environmental protection in accordance with [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2). For each determination of impracticability of secondary containment pursuant to [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d), the Plan must clearly explain why secondary containment measures are not practicable at this facility and provide the alternative measures required in [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d) in lieu of secondary containment. By certifying each measure allowed under [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and (d), the Professional Engineer attests:
  §viii-4-i-a (A) That he is familiar with the requirements of this part;
  §viii-4-i-b (B) That he or his agent has visited and examined the facility; and
  §viii-4-i-c (C) That the alternative method of environmental equivalence in accordance with [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) or the determination of impracticability and alternative measures in accordance with [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d) is consistent with good engineering practice, including consideration of applicable industry standards, and with the requirements of this part.
  §viii-4-ii (ii) As described in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, the facility owner or operator may not self-certify measures as described in [1dh] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping. Such measures must be reviewed and certified, in writing, by a licensed Professional Engineer, in accordance with [r2s] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d)(1)(vi).
  §viii-4-iii (iii) The review and certification by the Professional Engineer under this paragraph is limited to the alternative method which achieves equivalent environmental protection pursuant to [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2); to the impracticability determination and measures in lieu of secondary containment pursuant to [m4u] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d); or the measures pursuant to [1dh] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping and appurtenances downstream from the container.

<search shelf=wiki>As a Tier I warehouse our overfill rule stands in for the one in the onshore-facility section. That onshore section requires corrosion protection for completely buried metallic tanks installed on or after what date?</search>= 3 notes
  [5jk] page · 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities). — when: You need what section 112.8 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).
  [fde] page · 112.12 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements. — when: You need what section 112.12 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements.
  [ffe] page · 112.2 Definitions. — when: You need what section 112.2 requires: Definitions.
<open>5jk</open>= 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities). — Section 112.8 of the regulation — Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).
  §text If you are the owner or operator of an onshore facility (excluding a production facility), you must:
  §a (a) Meet the general requirements for the Plan listed under [adt] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., and the specific discharge prevention and containment procedures listed in this section.
  §b (b) Facility drainage. (1) Restrain drainage from diked storage areas by valves to prevent a discharge into the drainage system or facility effluent treatment system, except where facility systems are designed to control such discharge. You may empty diked areas by pumps or ejectors; however, you must manually activate these pumps or ejectors and must inspect the condition of the accumulation before starting, to ensure no oil will be discharged.
  §b-2 (2) Use valves of manual, open-and-closed design, for the drainage of diked areas. You may not use flapper-type drain valves to drain diked areas. If your facility drainage drains directly into a watercourse and not into an on-site wastewater treatment plant, you must inspect and may drain uncontaminated retained stormwater, as provided in paragraphs (c)(3)(ii), (iii), and (iv) of this section.
  §b-3 (3) Design facility drainage systems from undiked areas with a potential for a discharge (such as where piping is located outside containment walls or where tank truck discharges may occur outside the loading area) to flow into ponds, lagoons, or catchment basins designed to retain oil or return it to the facility. You must not locate catchment basins in areas subject to periodic flooding.
  §b-4 (4) If facility drainage is not engineered as in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, equip the final discharge of all ditches inside the facility with a diversion system that would, in the event of an uncontrolled discharge, retain oil in the facility.
  §b-5 (5) Where drainage waters are treated in more than one treatment unit and such treatment is continuous, and pump transfer is needed, provide two “lift” pumps and permanently install at least one of the pumps. Whatever techniques you use, you must engineer facility drainage systems to prevent a discharge as described in [8vy] 112.1 General applicability.(b) in case there is an equipment failure or human error at the facility.
  §c (c) Bulk storage containers. (1) Not use a container for the storage of oil unless its material and construction are compatible with the material stored and conditions of storage such as pressure and temperature.
  §c-2 (2) Construct all bulk storage tank installations (except mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks) so that you provide a secondary means of containment for the entire capacity of the largest single container and sufficient freeboard to contain precipitation. You must ensure that diked areas are sufficiently impervious to contain discharged oil. Dikes, containment curbs, and pits are commonly employed for this purpose. You may also use an alternative system consisting of a drainage trench enclosure that must be arranged so that any discharge will terminate and be safely confined in a facility catchment basin or holding pond.
  §c-3 (3) Not allow drainage of uncontaminated rainwater from the diked area into a storm drain or discharge of an effluent into an open watercourse, lake, or pond, bypassing the facility treatment system unless you:
  §c-3-i (i) Normally keep the bypass valve sealed closed.
  §c-3-ii (ii) Inspect the retained rainwater to ensure that its presence will not cause a discharge as described in [8vy] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §c-3-iii (iii) Open the bypass valve and reseal it following drainage under responsible supervision; and
  §c-3-iv (iv) Keep adequate records of such events, for example, any records required under permits issued in accordance with §§ 122.41(j)(2) and 122.41(m)(3) of this chapter.
  §c-4 (4) Protect any completely buried metallic storage tank installed on or after January 10, 1974 from corrosion by coatings or cathodic protection compatible with local soil conditions. You must regularly leak test such completely buried metallic storage tanks.
  §c-5 (5) Not use partially buried or bunkered metallic tanks for the storage of oil, unless you protect the buried section of the tank from corrosion. You must protect partially buried and bunkered tanks from corrosion by coatings or cathodic protection compatible with local soil conditions.
  §c-6 (6) Test or inspect each aboveground container for integrity on a regular schedule and whenever you make material repairs. You must determine, in accordance with industry standards, the appropriate qualifications for personnel performing tests and inspections, the frequency and type of testing and inspections, which take into account container size, configuration, and design (such as containers that are: shop-built, field-erected, skid-mounted, elevated, equipped with a liner, double-walled, or partially buried). Examples of these integrity tests include, but are not limited to: visual inspection, hydrostatic testing, radiographic testing, ultrasonic testing, acoustic emissions testing, or other systems of non-destructive testing. You must keep comparison records and you must also inspect the container's supports and foundations. In addition, you must frequently inspect the outside of the container for signs of deterioration, discharges, or accumulation of oil inside diked areas. Records of inspections and tests kept under usual and customary business practices satisfy the recordkeeping requirements of this paragraph.
  §c-7 (7) Control leakage through defective internal heating coils by monitoring the steam return and exhaust lines for contamination from internal heating coils that discharge into an open watercourse, or pass the steam return or exhaust lines through a settling tank, skimmer, or other separation or retention system.
  §c-8 (8) Engineer or update each container installation in accordance with good engineering practice to avoid discharges. You must provide at least one of the following devices:
  §c-8-i (i) High liquid level alarms with an audible or visual signal at a constantly attended operation or surveillance station. In smaller facilities an audible air vent may suffice.
  §c-8-ii (ii) High liquid level pump cutoff devices set to stop flow at a predetermined container content level.
  §c-8-iii (iii) Direct audible or code signal communication between the container gauger and the pumping station.
  §c-8-iv (iv) A fast response system for determining the liquid level of each bulk storage container such as digital computers, telepulse, or direct vision gauges. If you use this alternative, a person must be present to monitor gauges and the overall filling of bulk storage containers.
  §c-8-v (v) You must regularly test liquid level sensing devices to ensure proper operation.
  §c-9 (9) Observe effluent treatment facilities frequently enough to detect possible system upsets that could cause a discharge as described in [8vy] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §c-10 (10) Promptly correct visible discharges which result in a loss of oil from the container, including but not limited to seams, gaskets, piping, pumps, valves, rivets, and bolts. You must promptly remove any accumulations of oil in diked areas.
  §c-11 (11) Position or locate mobile or portable oil storage containers to prevent a discharge as described in [8vy] 112.1 General applicability.(b). Except for mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks, you must furnish a secondary means of containment, such as a dike or catchment basin, sufficient to contain the capacity of the largest single compartment or container with sufficient freeboard to contain precipitation.
  §d (d) Facility transfer operations, pumping, and facility process. (1) Provide buried piping that is installed or replaced on or after August 16, 2002, with a protective wrapping and coating. You must also cathodically protect such buried piping installations or otherwise satisfy the corrosion protection standards for piping in part 280 of this chapter or a State program approved under part 281 of this chapter. If a section of buried line is exposed for any reason, you must carefully inspect it for deterioration. If you find corrosion damage, you must undertake additional examination and corrective action as indicated by the magnitude of the damage.
  §d-2 (2) Cap or blank-flange the terminal connection at the transfer point and mark it as to origin when piping is not in service or is in standby service for an extended time.
  §d-3 (3) Properly design pipe supports to minimize abrasion and corrosion and allow for expansion and contraction.
  §d-4 (4) Regularly inspect all aboveground valves, piping, and appurtenances. During the inspection you must assess the general condition of items, such as flange joints, expansion joints, valve glands and bodies, catch pans, pipeline supports, locking of valves, and metal surfaces. You must also conduct integrity and leak testing of buried piping at the time of installation, modification, construction, relocation, or replacement.
  §d-5 (5) Warn all vehicles entering the facility to be sure that no vehicle will endanger aboveground piping or other oil transfer operations.
January 10, 1974 [5jk§c-4]

<search shelf=wiki>We are amending our self-certified Plan for a technical change, and the amendment rule sends qualified facilities to their own section instead of a Professional Engineer. We are Tier I: installing a container larger than what capacity takes us out of Tier I?</search>= 3 notes
  [jsz] page · 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements. — when: You need what section 112.6 requires: Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.
  [n0q] page · 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan. — when: You need what section 112.3 requires: Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.
  [g4i] page · 112.5 Amendment of Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan by owners or operators. — when: You need what section 112.5 requires: Amendment of Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan by owners or operators.
<open>n0q</open>= 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan. — Section 112.3 of the regulation — Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.
  §text The owner or operator or an onshore or offshore facility subject to this section must prepare in writing and implement a Spill Prevention Control and Countermeasure Plan (hereafter “SPCC Plan” or “Plan”),” in accordance with [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and any other applicable section of this part.
  §a (a)(1) Except as otherwise provided in this section, if your facility, or mobile or portable facility, was in operation on or before August 16, 2002, you must maintain your Plan, but must amend it, if necessary to ensure compliance with this part, and implement the amended Plan no later than November 10, 2011. If such a facility becomes operational after August 16, 2002, through November 10, 2011, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan on or before November 10, 2011. If such a facility (excluding oil production facilities) becomes operational after November 10, 2011, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan before you begin operations. You are not required to prepare a new Plan each time you move a mobile or portable facility to a new site; the Plan may be general. When you move the mobile or portable facility, you must locate and install it using the discharge prevention practices outlined in the Plan for the facility. The Plan is applicable only while the mobile or portable facility is in a fixed (non-transportation) operating mode.
  §a-2 (2) If your drilling, production or workover facility, including a mobile or portable facility, is offshore or has an offshore component; or your onshore facility is required to have and submit a Facility Response Plan pursuant to 40 CFR 112.20(a), and was in operation on or before August 16, 2002, you must maintain your Plan, but must amend it, if necessary to ensure compliance with this part, and implement the amended Plan no later than November 10, 2010. If such a facility becomes operational after August 16, 2002, through November 10, 2010, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan on or before November 10, 2010. If such a facility (excluding oil production facilities) becomes operational after November 10, 2010, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan before you begin operations. You are not required to prepare a new Plan each time you move a mobile or portable facility to a new site; the Plan may be general. When you move the mobile or portable facility, you must locate and install it using the discharge prevention practices outlined in the Plan for the facility. The Plan is applicable only while the mobile or portable facility is in a fixed (non-transportation) operating mode.
  §a-3 (3) If your farm, as defined in [kd2] 112.2 Definitions., was in operation on or before August 16, 2002, you must maintain your Plan, but must amend it, if necessary to ensure compliance with this part, and implement the amended Plan on or before May 10, 2013. If your farm becomes operational after August 16, 2002, through May 10, 2013, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan on or before May 10, 2013. If your farm becomes operational after May 10, 2013, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan before you begin operations.
  §b (b) If your oil production facility as described in paragraph (a)(1) of this section becomes operational after November 10, 2011, or as described in paragraph (a)(2) of this section becomes operational after November 10, 2010, and could reasonably be expected to have a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), you must prepare and implement a Plan within six months after you begin operations.
  §c (c) [Reserved]
  §d (d) Except as provided in [jsz] 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements., a licensed Professional Engineer must review and certify a Plan for it to be effective to satisfy the requirements of this part.
  §d-1 (1) By means of this certification the Professional Engineer attests:
  §d-1-i (i) That he is familiar with the requirements of this part ;
  §d-1-ii (ii) That he or his agent has visited and examined the facility;
  §d-1-iii (iii) That the Plan has been prepared in accordance with good engineering practice, including consideration of applicable industry standards, and with the requirements of this part;
  §d-1-iv (iv) That procedures for required inspections and testing have been established; and
  §d-1-v (v) That the Plan is adequate for the facility.
  §d-1-vi (vi) That, if applicable, for a produced water container subject to [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6), any procedure to minimize the amount of free-phase oil is designed to reduce the accumulation of free-phase oil and the procedures and frequency for required inspections, maintenance and testing have been established and are described in the Plan.
  §d-2 (2) Such certification shall in no way relieve the owner or operator of a facility of his duty to prepare and fully implement such Plan in accordance with the requirements of this part.
  §e (e) If you are the owner or operator of a facility for which a Plan is required under this section, you must:
  §e-1 (1) Maintain a complete copy of the Plan at the facility if the facility is normally attended at least four hours per day, or at the nearest field office if the facility is not so attended, and
  §e-2 (2) Have the Plan available to the Regional Administrator for on-site review during normal working hours.
  §f (f) Extension of time. (1) The Regional Administrator may authorize an extension of time for the preparation and full implementation of a Plan, or any amendment thereto, beyond the time permitted for the preparation, implementation, or amendment of a Plan under this part, when he finds that the owner or operator of a facility subject to this section, cannot fully comply with the requirements as a result of either nonavailability of qualified personnel, or delays in construction or equipment delivery beyond the control and without the fault of such owner or operator or his agents or employees.
  §f-2 (2) If you are an owner or operator seeking an extension of time under paragraph (f)(1) of this section, you may submit a written extension request to the Regional Administrator. Your request must include:
  §f-2-i (i) A full explanation of the cause for any such delay and the specific aspects of the Plan affected by the delay;
  §f-2-ii (ii) A full discussion of actions being taken or contemplated to minimize or mitigate such delay; and
  §f-2-iii (iii) A proposed time schedule for the implementation of any corrective actions being taken or contemplated, including interim dates for completion of tests or studies, installation and operation of any necessary equipment, or other preventive measures. In addition you may present additional oral or written statements in support of your extension request.
  §f-3 (3) The submission of a written extension request under paragraph (f)(2) of this section does not relieve you of your obligation to comply with the requirements of this part. The Regional Administrator may request a copy of your Plan to evaluate the extension request. When the Regional Administrator authorizes an extension of time for particular equipment or other specific aspects of the Plan, such extension does not affect your obligation to comply with the requirements related to other equipment or other specific aspects of the Plan for which the Regional Administrator has not expressly authorized an extension.
  §g (g) Qualified Facilities. The owner or operator of a qualified facility as defined in this subparagraph may self-certify his facility's Plan, as provided in [jsz] 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.. A qualified facility is one that meets the following Tier I or Tier II qualified facility criteria:
  §g-1 (1) A Tier I qualified facility meets the qualification criteria in paragraph (g)(2) of this section and has no individual aboveground oil storage container with a capacity greater than 5,000 U.S. gallons.
  §g-2 (2) A Tier II qualified facility is one that has had no single discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b) exceeding 1,000 U.S. gallons or no two discharges as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b) each exceeding 42 U.S. gallons within any twelve month period in the three years prior to the SPCC Plan self-certification date, or since becoming subject to this part if the facility has been in operation for less than three years (other than discharges as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b) that are the result of natural disasters, acts of war, or terrorism), and has an aggregate aboveground oil storage capacity of 10,000 U.S. gallons or less.
<open>jsz</open>= 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements. — Section 112.6 of the regulation — Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.
  §text Qualified facilities meeting the Tier I applicability criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1) are subject to the requirements in paragraph (a) of this section. Qualified facilities meeting the Tier II applicability criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2) are subject to the requirements in paragraph (b) of this section.
  §a (a) Tier I Qualified Facilities—(1) Preparation and Self-Certification of the Plan. If you are an owner or operator of a facility that meets the Tier I qualified facility criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1), you must either: comply with the requirements of paragraph (a)(3) of this section; or prepare and implement a Plan meeting requirements of paragraph (b) of this section; or prepare and implement a Plan meeting the general Plan requirements in [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and applicable requirements in subparts B and C, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d). If you do not follow the appendix G template, you must prepare an equivalent Plan that meets all of the applicable requirements listed in this part, and you must supplement it with a section cross-referencing the location of requirements listed in this part and the equivalent requirements in the other prevention plan. To complete the template in appendix G, you must certify that:
  §i (i) You are familiar with the applicable requirements of 40 CFR part 112;
  §ii (ii) You have visited and examined the facility;
  §iii (iii) You prepared the Plan in accordance with accepted and sound industry practices and standards;
  §iv (iv) You have established procedures for required inspections and testing in accordance with industry inspection and testing standards or recommended practices;
  §v (v) You will fully implement the Plan;
  §vi (vi) The facility meets the qualification criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1);
  §vii (vii) The Plan does not deviate from any requirement of this part as allowed by [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and 112.7(d) or include measures pursuant to [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping; and
  §viii (viii) The Plan and individual(s) responsible for implementing this Plan have the approval of management, and the facility owner or operator has committed the necessary resources to fully implement this Plan.
  §viii-2 (2) Technical Amendments. You must certify any technical amendments to your Plan in accordance with paragraph (a)(1) of this section when there is a change in the facility design, construction, operation, or maintenance that affects its potential for a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b). If the facility change results in the facility no longer meeting the Tier I qualifying criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(1) because an individual oil storage container capacity exceeds 5,000 U.S. gallons or the facility capacity exceeds 10,000 U.S. gallons in aggregate aboveground storage capacity, within six months following preparation of the amendment, you must either:
  §viii-2-i (i) Prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with [jsz] 112.6 Qualified Facilities Plan Requirements.(b) if you meet the Tier II qualified facility criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2); or
  §viii-2-ii (ii) Prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with the general Plan requirements in [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., and applicable requirements in subparts B and C, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d).
  §viii-3 (3) Plan Template and Applicable Requirements. Prepare and implement an SPCC Plan that meets the following requirements under [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and in subparts B and C of this part: introductory paragraph of §[wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., 112.7(a)(3)(i), 112.7(a)(3)(iv), 112.7(a)(3)(vi), 112.7(a)(4), 112.7(a)(5), 112.7(c), 112.7(e), 112.7(f), 112.7(g), 112.7(k), 112.8(b)(1), 112.8(b)(2), 112.8(c)(1), 112.8(c)(3), 112.8(c)(4), 112.8(c)(5), 112.8(c)(6), 112.8(c)(10), 112.8(d)(4), 112.9(b), 112.9(c)(1), 112.9(c)(2), 112.9(c)(3), 112.9(c)(4), 112.9(c)(5), 112.9(d)(1), 112.9(d)(3), 112.9(d)(4), 112.10(b), 112.10(c), 112.10(d), 112.12(b)(1), 112.12(b)(2), 112.12(c)(1), 112.12(c)(3), 112.12(c)(4), 112.12(c)(5), 112.12(c)(6), 112.12(c)(10), and 112.12(d)(4). The template in appendix G to this part has been developed to meet the requirements of 40 CFR part 112 and, when completed and signed by the owner or operator, may be used as the SPCC Plan. Additionally, you must meet the following requirements:
  §viii-3-i (i) Failure analysis, in lieu of the requirements in [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(b). Where experience indicates a reasonable potential for equipment failure (such as loading or unloading equipment, tank overflow, rupture, or leakage, or any other equipment known to be a source of discharge), include in your Plan a prediction of the direction and total quantity of oil which could be discharged from the facility as a result of each type of major equipment failure.
  §viii-3-ii (ii) Bulk storage container secondary containment, in lieu of the requirements in §[yun] 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).(c)(2) and (c)(11) and 112.12(c)(2) and (c)(11). Construct all bulk storage container installations (except mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks), including mobile or portable oil storage containers, so that you provide a secondary means of containment for the entire capacity of the largest single container plus additional capacity to contain precipitation. Dikes, containment curbs, and pits are commonly employed for this purpose. You may also use an alternative system consisting of a drainage trench enclosure that must be arranged so that any discharge will terminate and be safely confined in a catchment basin or holding pond. Position or locate mobile or portable oil storage containers to prevent a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §viii-3-iii (iii) Overfill prevention, in lieu of the requirements in §[yun] 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).(c)(8) and 112.12(c)(8). Ensure that each container is provided with a system or documented procedure to prevent overfills of the container, describe the system or procedure in the SPCC Plan and regularly test to ensure proper operation or efficacy.
  §b (b) Tier II Qualified Facilities—(1) Preparation and Self-Certification of Plan. If you are the owner or operator of a facility that meets the Tier II qualified facility criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2), you may choose to self-certify your Plan. You must certify in the Plan that:
  §i-2 (i) You are familiar with the requirements of this part;
  §ii-2 (ii) You have visited and examined the facility;
  §iii-2 (iii) The Plan has been prepared in accordance with accepted and sound industry practices and standards, and with the requirements of this part;
  §iv-2 (iv) Procedures for required inspections and testing have been established;
  §v-2 (v) You will fully implement the Plan;
  §vi-2 (vi) The facility meets the qualification criteria set forth under [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2);
  §vii-2 (vii) The Plan does not deviate from any requirement of this part as allowed by [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and 112.7(d) or include measures pursuant to [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping, except as provided in paragraph (b)(3) of this section; and
  §viii-4 (viii) The Plan and individual(s) responsible for implementing the Plan have the full approval of management and the facility owner or operator has committed the necessary resources to fully implement the Plan.
  §viii-2-2 (2) Technical Amendments. If you self-certify your Plan pursuant to paragraph (b)(1) of this section, you must certify any technical amendments to your Plan in accordance with paragraph (b)(1) of this section when there is a change in the facility design, construction, operation, or maintenance that affects its potential for a discharge as described in [20z] 112.1 General applicability.(b), except:
  §viii-2-i-2 (i) If a Professional Engineer certified a portion of your Plan in accordance with paragraph (b)(4) of this section, and the technical amendment affects this portion of the Plan, you must have the amended provisions of your Plan certified by a Professional Engineer in accordance with paragraph (b)(4)(ii) of this section.
  §viii-2-ii-2 (ii) If the change is such that the facility no longer meets the Tier II qualifying criteria in [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(g)(2) because it exceeds 10,000 U.S. gallons in aggregate aboveground storage capacity you must, within six months following the change, prepare and implement a Plan in accordance with the general Plan requirements in [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and the applicable requirements in subparts B and C of this part, including having the Plan certified by a Professional Engineer as required under [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d).
  §viii-3-2 (3) Applicable Requirements. Except as provided in this paragraph, your self-certified SPCC Plan must comply with [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans. and the applicable requirements in subparts B and C of this part:
  §viii-3-i-2 (i) Environmental Equivalence. Your Plan may not include alternate methods which provide environmental equivalence pursuant to [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2), unless each alternate method has been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-3-ii-2 (ii) Impracticability. Your Plan may not include any determinations that secondary containment is impracticable and provisions in lieu of secondary containment pursuant to [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d), unless each such determination and alternate measure has been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-3-iii-2 (iii) Produced Water Containers. Your Plan may not include any alternative procedures for skimming produced water containers in lieu of sized secondary containment pursuant to [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6), unless they have been reviewed and certified in writing by a Professional Engineer, as provided in paragraph (b)(4) of this section.
  §viii-4-2 (4) Professional Engineer Certification of Portions of a Qualified Facility's Self-Certified Plan.
  §viii-4-i (i) As described in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, the facility owner or operator may not self-certify alternative measures allowed under [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) or (d), that are included in the facility's Plan. Such measures must be reviewed and certified, in writing, by a licensed Professional Engineer. For each alternative measure allowed under [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2), the Plan must be accompanied by a written statement by a Professional Engineer that states the reason for nonconformance and describes the alternative method and how it provides equivalent environmental protection in accordance with [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2). For each determination of impracticability of secondary containment pursuant to [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d), the Plan must clearly explain why secondary containment measures are not practicable at this facility and provide the alternative measures required in [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d) in lieu of secondary containment. By certifying each measure allowed under [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) and (d), the Professional Engineer attests:
  §viii-4-i-a (A) That he is familiar with the requirements of this part;
  §viii-4-i-b (B) That he or his agent has visited and examined the facility; and
  §viii-4-i-c (C) That the alternative method of environmental equivalence in accordance with [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2) or the determination of impracticability and alternative measures in accordance with [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d) is consistent with good engineering practice, including consideration of applicable industry standards, and with the requirements of this part.
  §viii-4-ii (ii) As described in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, the facility owner or operator may not self-certify measures as described in [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping. Such measures must be reviewed and certified, in writing, by a licensed Professional Engineer, in accordance with [n0q] 112.3 Requirement to prepare and implement a Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan.(d)(1)(vi).
  §viii-4-iii (iii) The review and certification by the Professional Engineer under this paragraph is limited to the alternative method which achieves equivalent environmental protection pursuant to [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(a)(2); to the impracticability determination and measures in lieu of secondary containment pursuant to [wge] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans.(d); or the measures pursuant to [atf] 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).(c)(6) for produced water containers and any associated piping and appurtenances downstream from the container.

<search shelf=wiki>Our Tier I containment rule replaces the bulk-storage containment paragraphs of the onshore-facility section. In that onshore section, buried piping installed or replaced on or after what date needs a protective wrapping and coating?</search>= 3 notes
  [y3j] page · 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities). — when: You need what section 112.8 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).
  [zf1] page · 112.12 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements. — when: You need what section 112.12 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements.
  [zjk] page · 112.9 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities). — when: You need what section 112.9 requires: Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan Requirements for onshore oil production facilities (excluding drilling and workover facilities).
<open>y3j</open>= 112.8 Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities). — Section 112.8 of the regulation — Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plan requirements for onshore facilities (excluding production facilities).
  §text If you are the owner or operator of an onshore facility (excluding a production facility), you must:
  §a (a) Meet the general requirements for the Plan listed under [v7j] 112.7 General requirements for Spill Prevention, Control, and Countermeasure Plans., and the specific discharge prevention and containment procedures listed in this section.
  §b (b) Facility drainage. (1) Restrain drainage from diked storage areas by valves to prevent a discharge into the drainage system or facility effluent treatment system, except where facility systems are designed to control such discharge. You may empty diked areas by pumps or ejectors; however, you must manually activate these pumps or ejectors and must inspect the condition of the accumulation before starting, to ensure no oil will be discharged.
  §b-2 (2) Use valves of manual, open-and-closed design, for the drainage of diked areas. You may not use flapper-type drain valves to drain diked areas. If your facility drainage drains directly into a watercourse and not into an on-site wastewater treatment plant, you must inspect and may drain uncontaminated retained stormwater, as provided in paragraphs (c)(3)(ii), (iii), and (iv) of this section.
  §b-3 (3) Design facility drainage systems from undiked areas with a potential for a discharge (such as where piping is located outside containment walls or where tank truck discharges may occur outside the loading area) to flow into ponds, lagoons, or catchment basins designed to retain oil or return it to the facility. You must not locate catchment basins in areas subject to periodic flooding.
  §b-4 (4) If facility drainage is not engineered as in paragraph (b)(3) of this section, equip the final discharge of all ditches inside the facility with a diversion system that would, in the event of an uncontrolled discharge, retain oil in the facility.
  §b-5 (5) Where drainage waters are treated in more than one treatment unit and such treatment is continuous, and pump transfer is needed, provide two “lift” pumps and permanently install at least one of the pumps. Whatever techniques you use, you must engineer facility drainage systems to prevent a discharge as described in [r92] 112.1 General applicability.(b) in case there is an equipment failure or human error at the facility.
  §c (c) Bulk storage containers. (1) Not use a container for the storage of oil unless its material and construction are compatible with the material stored and conditions of storage such as pressure and temperature.
  §c-2 (2) Construct all bulk storage tank installations (except mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks) so that you provide a secondary means of containment for the entire capacity of the largest single container and sufficient freeboard to contain precipitation. You must ensure that diked areas are sufficiently impervious to contain discharged oil. Dikes, containment curbs, and pits are commonly employed for this purpose. You may also use an alternative system consisting of a drainage trench enclosure that must be arranged so that any discharge will terminate and be safely confined in a facility catchment basin or holding pond.
  §c-3 (3) Not allow drainage of uncontaminated rainwater from the diked area into a storm drain or discharge of an effluent into an open watercourse, lake, or pond, bypassing the facility treatment system unless you:
  §c-3-i (i) Normally keep the bypass valve sealed closed.
  §c-3-ii (ii) Inspect the retained rainwater to ensure that its presence will not cause a discharge as described in [r92] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §c-3-iii (iii) Open the bypass valve and reseal it following drainage under responsible supervision; and
  §c-3-iv (iv) Keep adequate records of such events, for example, any records required under permits issued in accordance with §§ 122.41(j)(2) and 122.41(m)(3) of this chapter.
  §c-4 (4) Protect any completely buried metallic storage tank installed on or after January 10, 1974 from corrosion by coatings or cathodic protection compatible with local soil conditions. You must regularly leak test such completely buried metallic storage tanks.
  §c-5 (5) Not use partially buried or bunkered metallic tanks for the storage of oil, unless you protect the buried section of the tank from corrosion. You must protect partially buried and bunkered tanks from corrosion by coatings or cathodic protection compatible with local soil conditions.
  §c-6 (6) Test or inspect each aboveground container for integrity on a regular schedule and whenever you make material repairs. You must determine, in accordance with industry standards, the appropriate qualifications for personnel performing tests and inspections, the frequency and type of testing and inspections, which take into account container size, configuration, and design (such as containers that are: shop-built, field-erected, skid-mounted, elevated, equipped with a liner, double-walled, or partially buried). Examples of these integrity tests include, but are not limited to: visual inspection, hydrostatic testing, radiographic testing, ultrasonic testing, acoustic emissions testing, or other systems of non-destructive testing. You must keep comparison records and you must also inspect the container's supports and foundations. In addition, you must frequently inspect the outside of the container for signs of deterioration, discharges, or accumulation of oil inside diked areas. Records of inspections and tests kept under usual and customary business practices satisfy the recordkeeping requirements of this paragraph.
  §c-7 (7) Control leakage through defective internal heating coils by monitoring the steam return and exhaust lines for contamination from internal heating coils that discharge into an open watercourse, or pass the steam return or exhaust lines through a settling tank, skimmer, or other separation or retention system.
  §c-8 (8) Engineer or update each container installation in accordance with good engineering practice to avoid discharges. You must provide at least one of the following devices:
  §c-8-i (i) High liquid level alarms with an audible or visual signal at a constantly attended operation or surveillance station. In smaller facilities an audible air vent may suffice.
  §c-8-ii (ii) High liquid level pump cutoff devices set to stop flow at a predetermined container content level.
  §c-8-iii (iii) Direct audible or code signal communication between the container gauger and the pumping station.
  §c-8-iv (iv) A fast response system for determining the liquid level of each bulk storage container such as digital computers, telepulse, or direct vision gauges. If you use this alternative, a person must be present to monitor gauges and the overall filling of bulk storage containers.
  §c-8-v (v) You must regularly test liquid level sensing devices to ensure proper operation.
  §c-9 (9) Observe effluent treatment facilities frequently enough to detect possible system upsets that could cause a discharge as described in [r92] 112.1 General applicability.(b).
  §c-10 (10) Promptly correct visible discharges which result in a loss of oil from the container, including but not limited to seams, gaskets, piping, pumps, valves, rivets, and bolts. You must promptly remove any accumulations of oil in diked areas.
  §c-11 (11) Position or locate mobile or portable oil storage containers to prevent a discharge as described in [r92] 112.1 General applicability.(b). Except for mobile refuelers and other non-transportation-related tank trucks, you must furnish a secondary means of containment, such as a dike or catchment basin, sufficient to contain the capacity of the largest single compartment or container with sufficient freeboard to contain precipitation.
  §d (d) Facility transfer operations, pumping, and facility process. (1) Provide buried piping that is installed or replaced on or after August 16, 2002, with a protective wrapping and coating. You must also cathodically protect such buried piping installations or otherwise satisfy the corrosion protection standards for piping in part 280 of this chapter or a State program approved under part 281 of this chapter. If a section of buried line is exposed for any reason, you must carefully inspect it for deterioration. If you find corrosion damage, you must undertake additional examination and corrective action as indicated by the magnitude of the damage.
  §d-2 (2) Cap or blank-flange the terminal connection at the transfer point and mark it as to origin when piping is not in service or is in standby service for an extended time.
  §d-3 (3) Properly design pipe supports to minimize abrasion and corrosion and allow for expansion and contraction.
  §d-4 (4) Regularly inspect all aboveground valves, piping, and appurtenances. During the inspection you must assess the general condition of items, such as flange joints, expansion joints, valve glands and bodies, catch pans, pipeline supports, locking of valves, and metal surfaces. You must also conduct integrity and leak testing of buried piping at the time of installation, modification, construction, relocation, or replacement.
  §d-5 (5) Warn all vehicles entering the facility to be sure that no vehicle will endanger aboveground piping or other oil transfer operations.
August 16, 2002 [y3j§d]

<search shelf=wiki>After two spills within a year at our terminal we must report to the Regional Administrator, counting only discharges as described in the general-applicability section. Harmful quantities there are as described in which part of the chapter?</search>= 3 notes
